senses.gloss: how easily others can check it
senses.definition: Whether a claim can be checked by someone other than whoever made it.
senses.caution: People hear it as trustworthy, but a number can be easy to check and still wrong. Promise it only if you can say who checks it and against what.
senses.example: Our advantage isn't that the model is right more often, it's the verifiability — every number traces back to a filing.

cues.text: A compliance officer asks what makes AI output acceptable inside a regulated process, and your answer is that every figure traces back to a document anyone can open.
You are arguing for the design that shows its sources over the one that is more accurate but opaque.
A board member asks why you trust one vendor's numbers more than another's.
A friend forwards you a health claim, and you want a word for exactly what it lacks: no way for anyone outside to check it.
You are comparing two second-hand cars and one comes with a full documented service history.

distractors: The property of work that runs for many steps before anyone can tell whether it worked.
A voluntary group of people who do the same work and meet to trade what they learn.
The words a business actually uses mapped onto the raw tables underneath them.
Weight and seriousness in how a person carries themselves.
To decide as you go, taking your lead from how things develop.

gloss_distractors: how easily others can check it
senses.definition: Training signal a machine can check on its own, like a test passing or a proof compiling.
senses.caution: It only covers tasks with a checkable answer, so do not promise it for memos or judgement calls. Non-technical people may think it means a bonus scheme.
senses.example: Coding and maths get verifiable rewards for free. Nothing in our analyst workflow has an answer key like that.

cues.text: You are explaining why the newest models are so strong at code and so weak at the judgement work clients actually pay for, and the difference is whether a machine can mark the answer.
An MD asks what it would take to train a model on your internal process, and your first question is whether anything in it has a checkable right answer.
In a design session you want the term for the class of training signal that needs no human rater because correctness is mechanical.
You are pushing back on a plan to fine-tune on senior analysts' opinions, where nothing can be marked automatically.

distractors: The accumulated history an organisation holds about why its systems were built the way they were.
A voluntary group of people who do the same kind of work and meet to trade what they are learning.
The one outcome you steer by, held fixed while everything else stays negotiable.
A slice of the market defined by the industry it serves.
To work over the exact phrasing of something already written.
